subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should the shared reply pipeline suppress generic prefix text followed by `NO_REPLY`, or keep the current rule that only narrower token-only, reasoning-prefixed, and cron-specific cases suppress the whole payload?
rationale: Current source and tests deliberately preserve some substantive trailing-token replies, while this issue asks to convert that shape into full suppression for leak prevention; automation cannot safely choose the message-loss versus leak-prevention boundary.

options.title: Define Narrow Shared Suppression
options.body: Suppress whole messages for a maintainer-approved final-line or silent-intent boundary, document it, and add tests for both suppressed leaks and preserved substantive replies.

options.title: Adopt Broad Contains Suppression
options.body: Treat any `NO_REPLY` occurrence as a whole-message suppressor, accepting compatibility and message-loss risk for text that previously delivered after token stripping.

options.title: Preserve Current Split Behavior
options.body: Keep the reasoning-prefixed, punctuation token-only, and cron-specific fixes, then close or re-scope this request as not planned for generic mixed content.

recommendation.title: Define Narrow Shared Suppression
recommendation.body: Suppress whole messages for a maintainer-approved final-line or silent-intent boundary, document it, and add tests for both suppressed leaks and preserved substantive replies.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged partial fixes and the existing review route the shared suppression policy boundary to this reviewer/merger.
